items.title: Removed From 2,700 Theaters, ‘Street Fighter’ Officially Crawls Past Final Box-Office Milestone
items.summary: Video game adaptations had mixed results this year: The Super Mario Galaxy Movie and Resident Evil delivered massive box-office success, while two other films fell short of expectations. The first underperformer was Mortal Kombat II , a sequel to the quietly successful 2021 reboot, which grossed more than $80 million worldwide despite being part of the controversial "Project Popcorn" release strategy. Every film released under this strategy was released day-and-date on HBO Max and in theaters, greatly impacting its performance. Mortal Kombat II , on the other hand, failed to capitalize on its exclusive big-screen run. The second video game underperformer is more recent, and even less successful than Mortal Kombat II .

items.title: Jared Padalecki Reveals Why He Thinks ‘Gilmore Girls’ Made Dean So Unlikable [Exclusive]
items.summary: Even nearly 20 years after the series ended, every Gilmore Girls fan has their own opinion about Rory's ( Alexis Bledel ) boyfriends . Dean ( Jared Padalecki ), Jess ( Milo Ventimiglia ), and Logan ( Matt Czuchry ) all have iconic moments, but none is perfect, which is why the debate gets so heated. Yet, any fan, regardless of their favorite, must admit that Rory's first love, Dean, changed dramatically throughout the series. Introduced in the first episode , Dean is friendly, easygoing, and understanding, but as the series goes on, he exhibits more and more red flags, culminating in the infamous storyline where he cheats on his wife to sleep with Rory. items.title: Josephine review – Channing Tatum and Gemma Chan ballast knotty drama about a child witness to a rape
items.summary:
Mason Reeves steals the show as an eight year old who stumbles across a sex assault but, despite strong performances, parts of the film feel contrived

Beth de Araújo’s new movie takes a very big swing, and it has won prizes and acclaim since its premiere at Sundance. I was unsure about some of the film’s high-concept ideas but the lead performance from its eight-year-old newcomer Mason Reeves is outstanding. Those concerned about spoilers had better look away.

Channing Tatum and Gemma Chan play Damien and Claire, a smart professional couple in San Francisco with a bright young daughter called Josephine, marvellously played by Reeves. Damien takes Josephine to Golden Gate Park one morning to play football (they turn out to enjoy watching the English Premier League on TV). She mischievously runs on ahead of her dad to a secluded spot in the park where Damien can’t immediately find her and it is there that Josephine witnesses a rape – not less horrifying for being filmed in long shot.

Continue reading...

items.title: From Dumb Starbucks to dada documentary: everything you need to know about Nathan Fielder
items.summary:
With the UK release of You Can See Everything looming, now’s an ideal time to get up to speed on the bizarre, puckish and very meta comedic oeuvre of its star

“There are three sides to every story: your side, my side, and the truth. And no one is lying. Memories shared serve each differently.” Those words were spoken by film producer Robert Evans – but nobody has ever interrogated the idea more skilfully than comedian Nathan Fielder.

The three-hour documentary You Can See Everything – co-directed by and starring Fielder – opens in the UK on Friday, having already become an unlikely cultural phenomenon and box office sensation in the US. The film follows disgraced Theranos founder Elizabeth Holmes in the weeks leading up to her beginning a prison sentence for defrauding investors; what emerges is a profound meditation on the nature of truth and the fundamental unknowability of other human beings. To view the film as being simply about the Theranos scandal is akin to considering Casablanca merely a movie about a nightclub. And, as one might expect given Fielder’s background, it’s hilarious.

Continue reading...
items.t: From Dumb Starbucks to dada documentary: everything you need to know about Nathan Fielder

items.title: Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother review – Mahershala Ali’s religious hitman on the hunt for baby milk
items.summary:
The Oscar-winner plays a Muslim contract killer in a boisterous, blackly comic thriller with shades of John Woo and Tarantino

There are shades of John Woo and Tarantino here in a black-comic thriller from Pakistani-American director Bassam Tariq. There are shades also of Blade, the Marvel character that this film’s star, Mahershala Ali, had been preparing to play in a planned but then cancelled MCU movie which Tariq was going to direct. Here Ali plays Latif, a military veteran turned hitman for hire who uses knives and swords, not guns, and just happens to be a devout Muslim. The title refers to the Islamic tradition in which Muhammad was asked three times who is the most deserving of respect and replied each time: “Your mother.” It is, however, this film’s semi-intentional irony that mothers and female authority figures are largely irrelevant in it, the drama being more about men without women.

Latif is just finishing off a chaotic wet job in a squalid public bathroom one day, when he takes a call on his mobile from his teenage daughter Fatiha (played by Adia, from Steven Soderbergh’s streaming series Full Circle) telling him that his wife, Fatiha’s mother, has died. Convulsed with guilt at having neglected the family home for his homicidal profession, Latif arrives back to find his son Qadir (Jahleel Kamara) acting out, and his newborn baby allergic to formula, and only able to drink the expressed breast milk of which his late wife has left a limited stockpile in…

items.title: ‘The aesthetics in my family were so high, I felt ugly’: Charlotte Gainsbourg on extremism, abortion and her mother, Jane Birkin
items.summary:
In her new film, the actor plays a lawyer taking on the French state over reproductive rights. She talks about being criticised for her support of Israel and pushed to the limit by Lars von Trier

While she was making the film Women on Trial, about the real-life trial of a child prosecuted for having an abortion, someone sent Charlotte Gainsbourg a photograph of her mother at one of the pro-choice demonstrations that erupted in France at the time. It was “very moving”, says Gainsbourg to see her mother, the actor Jane Birkin, in 1972, “looking beautiful and in the middle of a demonstration”. At that time, in a court in Bobigny, a Paris suburb, the prominent lawyer Gisèle Halimi was defending 16-year-old Marie-Claire Chevalier, as well as her mother and two other women who helped her have an abortion, then illegal in France.

The Bobigny trial was new to her, says Gainsbourg, who plays Halimi, a leading figure in French feminism and activism who died in 2020. “I had no idea. For me, abortion rights started with Simone Veil” – the French minister of health who saw through decriminalisation three years later – “so I had to catch up.”

Continue reading...
items.t: ‘The aesthetics in my family were so high, I felt ugly’: Charlotte Gainsbourg on extremism, abortion and her mother, Jane Birkin

items.title: Robert Pattinson’s gift for cool, sensual menace makes him an exquisite choice as James Bond | Peter Bradshaw
items.summary:
Pattinson is a character actor whose talent for inscrutable appraisal may mean a new era for 007. Will this more willowy, classy Bond leave sexism in the shadows?

• New James Bond announced ... and the name’s Pattinson, Robert Pattinson
• Share your thoughts on the casting
• Pattinson’s journey from Harry Potter and Twilight to James Bond

If it wasn’t Bond … maybe it would have been Dr No in some hi-tech reboot. But Robert Pattinson – with his movie-star chops and track record in hip A24-type character turns, and his gift for cool, inscrutable appraisal and sensual menace – is an exquisite choice as 007, playing on the darker and more sophisticated notes of Pattinson’s performing personality.

And let’s hope, incidentally, that the actor now isn’t forced into a five-hour daily gym regimen to bulk up. I like the taller and more willowy Bond that Pattinson represents, the Bond from whose frame the tux hangs gracefully, the Bond with elegant abandon who’s a former British Naval officer, not a former US Navy Seal, the Bond who with a crinkly-eyed reptilian grin can style out waking up with a hangover after too many whisky-and-sodas at the baccarat table.
items.t: Robert Pattinson’s gift for cool, sensual menace makes him an exquisite choice as James Bond | Peter Bradshaw

items.title: The DCU’s James Gunn and Peter Safran are out – this is the biggest disaster to hit superhero movies in years
items.summary:
The adventurous weirdness of the Gunn/Safran era that fans responded to is now history. Can the DCU ever get back on track?

What was Warner Bros’ plan in 2022, when the studio decided to reboot its superhero output, jettison the increasingly muddled DC Extended Universe (DCEU) and replace it with a sparkling new DC Universe (DCU)? In part it was to wipe the slate clean after years of false starts, abandoned storylines and tonal lurches. There was a little bit of Marvel envy to proceedings, and quite possibly a desire to avoid having to ever again discuss Batman v Superman: Dawn of Justice’s numerous failings. But mostly it was to take advantage of hiring of a man whom nobody could accuse of being short of ideas on how to make comic book movies. To a greater or lesser extent, the plan was James Gunn.

Fast forward four years, and that plan lies in tatters. Gunn and his fellow DC Studios CEO Peter Safran have this week been fired (though they will reportedly stay on as film-makers), and Jeremy Latcham, another former Marvel man, is the new boss. What is the plan now? Nobody seems to know, and there is not much point asking David Ellison, the man whose Skydance empire has now gobbled up two of the former big five Hollywood studios (Paramount last year and Warner…
items.t: The DCU’s James Gunn and Peter Safran are out – this is the biggest disaster to hit superhero movies in years
